reconstruction.stage_saved: Use stored J and Q directly; do not replace auxiliary J with a physical solve from m.
reconstruction.from_coefficients: S=Us diag(sig) Vh; r=count(sig>0.001*sig[0]); Vd=Vh[:r].conj().T; JD=Vd@((Us[:,:r].conj().T@Y)/sig[:r,None]); construct U with original fourier_apcs(shape,mf,Vd); J=JD+U@A; Q=E0+G@J. This requires SVD/basis arithmetic, not a Maxwell material solve; not executed in this inventory.
reconstruction.confirmation_candidate_m: candidate_m rows 0,1,2,3 are initial host, stage0,stage1,stage2 in validate append order; these do not determine off-shell auxiliary J.
reconstruction.final_j: final lowercase j/Q are exact Maxwell fields at selected final material; they are not joint auxiliary stage states.

replay_requirements.old_stage_diagnostics: No replay needed for m/J/Q at saved stage ends; use metadata from matching AUXILIARY history stage_end.
replay_requirements.old_boundary_restart: Next stage can start from saved m and A using original frequency zero-padding; PR is reset at stage boundaries. Exact numerical reproduction remains environment-dependent.
replay_requirements.old_interior_trajectory: Replay only auxiliary stages to requested point; no corrector needed. Save pre-current m/A plus PR old_grad/old_direction if exact interior restart is required.
replay_requirements.confirmation_stage_states: Replay auxiliary only from public host m0 and original frozen config because only stage m survived. Stop at needed stage; do not rerun corrector to obtain auxiliary state.
replay_requirements.callback_gap: Existing iteration_callback exposes post-readout m/J/A; stage_callback exposes m/J/Q/A at stage ends. A wrapper can retain previous callback m (initial host before first call) for m_before and reconstruct Q=E0+G@J at predetermined checkpoints only. No solver edit needed for these diagnostics. old_grad/old_direction remain unavailable for exact interior PR restart.
replay_requirements.absent_controls: phase_pi/self on confirmation cases have no saved run; cannot be called replay. A new control execution requires explicit separate scope and cost.
